findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling passkeys on initial login
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, `authenticate()` and `challenge()` filled the WebAuthn conditional UI data whenever passkeys were enabled and no user was selected yet.

Now, on a normal first login (no user in the context), `fillContextForm` is never called. The conditional passkey UI therefore disappears from the username/password form, which is the main passkeys use case. The check looks inverted or wrongly scoped: the intent was likely to always allow passkeys when enabled.

The initial-login tests that assert the `webauth` form is present should fail with this change.

findings.title: UsernameForm calls an isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() overload that does not exist
findings.body:
`UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The superclass only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, so this does not compile.

It should probably pass `context.getUser()` or call a separate check of whether passkeys are enabled.
